rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: **Coulomb's law.** The force between two point charges is directly proportional to the product of the charges and inversely proportional to the square of the distance: F = (1/4πε₀)q₁q₂/r².  ·  **Direction.** The force acts along the line joining the charges — repulsive for like charges, attractive for unlike charges — and obeys Newton's third law.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Potential V = kq/r; ΔV = W/q; U of a charge in potential = qV. Equipotential surfaces are ⟂ to field lines.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: **Permittivity.** In a medium of dielectric constant K the force falls to F = q₁q₂/4πε₀Kr²; for vacuum K = 1 and ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² C² N⁻¹ m⁻².  ·  **Vector form.** F₁₂ = (q₁q₂/4πε₀) × (r₂ − r₁)/|r₂ − r₁|³ gives both magnitude and direction automatically, with the sign of the charges deciding attraction or repulsion.  ·  **Limitations.** The law holds for point charges at rest and for spherically symmetric charge distributions; it is an inverse-square law like gravitation but far stronger.
